title: Find out whether a Forever motion shorter than the loop stutters
goal: Every motion in an icon shares one loop as long as the longest motion, and a motion that ends early holds still until the loop starts over. Reading the code says a spinner set to Forever at 800 ms beside a 900 ms bell pauses for a tenth of a second every turn, on the canvas and in the exported SVG, which breaks the promise that a spinner loops with no stutter. Check it, and if it is so, make a Forever motion repeat at its own pace.
notes: Not reproduced in the app: code reading only, hence p2 look-into. One shared cycle: Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerMotion.swift motionCycleLengthMS / automaticMotionCycleLengthMS ~1525-1550 (deliberately ONE CYCLE, see comment and MotionStrip.swift). A motion that ends early holds its final value (~1006). SVG export writes the same cycle length: Sources/PhotonzCore/SVGMotionExport.swift ~311; in SVG each animate element can carry its own dur with repeatCount=indefinite. Mock icon-loop-wt.html: 'with Forever on it, a length becomes a rate'.
acceptance: The case is run: one frame with a bell at its default 900 ms rotation and a spinner 0 to 360 degrees, Linear, Forever, 800 ms; the result (canvas and exported SVG in a browser) is written into this task's log with how it was measured
If the spinner pauses: a Forever motion repeats at its own length on the canvas and in the exported SVG, the timing strip shows that honestly, and a walk covers it at Next defaults
If it does not pause: the task closes with the evidence and no code change
Audit written under queue/audits/ if the app changed; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not
